summary: Live console widget time window jumps on 'Continue' during long-running query
description:
Issue summary: Several enterprise customers report that the 'Live' time-series widget (console dashboard) unexpectedly shifts its displayed time window when an operator clicks 'Continue' to resume results for a long-running query. Impact: Dashboards skip forward/backwards by up to 5 minutes, missing data points and causing alert threshold misfires. This appears after the 2026-03-09 frontend throttle debounce change.

Observed behavior: While a query that runs >60s is executing, pressing the 'Continue' button on the live panel causes the time window to jump to an earlier range (typically subtracting the panel interval) or stutter forward on subsequent resumes. Alerts attached to the panel either fire spuriously or fail to evaluate expected recent samples.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Open a dashboard with a Live panel set to '1m' refresh and time window 'Last 5m'.
2) Trigger a long-running ad-hoc query (simulate by forcing backend sleep on a dev branch or using a heavy aggregated query) that takes >60 seconds to respond.
3) While the panel is waiting, click 'Pause' then 'Continue' repeatedly, or click 'Continue' after the query completes.
4) Observe that the panel's visible time range jumps (visible x-axis moving earlier) and data that should be in the window is omitted.
5) Check alert evaluation history for the attached rule and note mismatched timestamps.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: race between the frontend's 'continue' handler and live-subscription resubscribe path that reuses a cached 'lastSeen' timeRange value. The debounced update from the 2026-03-09 deploy may have changed when the client requests an explicit new range vs reusing a stale window. Frontend changes touched code around subscription unmount/remount and debounce; see PR 4123. Reproduced on staging when toggling debounce_off flag. Query-service returns correct samples; the mismatch appears to be introduced by an incorrect 'from' timestamp sent by the client on re-subscribe. SRE confirmed no drop in websocket messages at proxy level.
Action items: add server-side validation to clamp re-subscribe ranges to 'now' when live=true; add telemetry to log requested range on subscribe; revert debounce change behind feature flag if needed.
comments: [2026-03-10T16:05:00Z] Support - Elena Park: A BrightRoute engineer reported dashboards for two orgs. Attached a screenshot and the request IDs above. Customer sees alerts firing for old buckets.

[2026-03-11T09:22:00Z] Frontend - Marc O'Neill: Reproduced locally with feature flag debounce_on. Suspect stale lastSeen is read from panel store when unmounting. Preparing a quick patch to set lastSeen = now() on explicit 'continue' for live panels.
[2026-03-11T13:40:00Z] SRE - Anika Das: No proxy errors found. Websocket keepalive steady. Confirmed subscribe messages include older 'from' values when client resumes.

[2026-03-12T10:10:00Z] Support - Elena Park: Customer confirmed workaround (refresh dashboard tab) restores correct behavior; they requested ETA on fix and whether alerts retroactively evaluate missed samples.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided: refresh the dashboard tab or toggle live interval. Patch in review: console-ui PR 4128 will force re-subscribe with range anchored to now() when live panels are resumed. If validated, schedule hotfix release to prod with monitoring for alert evaluation anomalies. Follow-up: add an automated test and a dashboard-level telemetry metric for subscribe ranges to prevent regressions.
